item.title: Papua New Guinea and Niue sign framework agreement
item.description: Papua New Guinea and Niue have signed a framework agreement on development and technical cooperation. The deal sets out a framework for cooperation in areas such as economic development, technical assistance and capacity building.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea and Niue have signed a framework agreement on development and technical cooperation.

The deal sets out a framework for cooperation in areas such as economic development, technical assistance and capacity building.

The agreement was signed between Prime Minister James Marape and Niue PM Dalton Tagelagi on the sidelines of the 55th Pacific Islands Forum leaders’ meeting in Koror, Palau.

PM Marape said the agreement reflects PNG's commitment to strengthening cooperation within the Pacific family and sharing knowledge, expertise and resources.

He explains the framework provides an overarching mechanism through, which the two countries can develop specific programs according to key priorities.

The agreement identifies a range of areas from trade, investment, tourism, economic cooperation, education, labour mobility, renewable energy, digital connectivity and people to people exchanges.

PM Marape says the agreement also complements the 2050 strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent by strengthening partnerships in the region and building greater resilience and self-reliance.

In the meantime, the framework, whilst in effect, can be terminated if either country gives six months' notice.

item.title: Pacific Ocean is at risk of climate threats
item.description: Pacific Leaders are calling for urgent action as Pacific Ocean is at risk if global warming exceeds 1.5 degrees Celsius. Vanutau's Minister for Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management Ralph Regenvanu said this when addressing the media, during the leaders meeting in Koror, Palau, recently.
item.content:encoded:
Pacific Leaders are calling for urgent action as Pacific Ocean is at risk if global warming exceeds 1.5 degrees Celsius.

Vanutau's Minister for Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management Ralph Regenvanu said this when addressing the media, during the leaders meeting in Koror, Palau, recently.

“We know that greenhouse gas emissions come from fossil fuels and we must urgently accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels.” Regenvanu said.

He reminded all states that the International Court of Justice's advisory opinion identified the collective temperature goal as being of holding the global average temperature to 1.5 degrees Celsius, above pre-industrial levels.

“This is recognised by the court. If emissions are not rapidly reduced in the next four years, any overshoot of 1.5 degrees Celsius will grow in both duration and severity, intensifying climate impacts and increasing loss and damage for all our communities in the Pacific.” He said.

Minister Regenvanu made a call to the oil producing countries to fossil fuel that they need the political will to transition away from fossil fuels.

item.title: NBC in conflict reporting
item.description: The National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] is boosting its capacity for conflict reporting, as the spread of misinformation and disinformation becomes the biggest threat to credible news. The NBC has nominated one of its senior journalists for the War Journalism Training Programme in Türkiye this month.
item.content:encoded:
The National Broadcasting Corporation [NBC] is boosting its capacity for conflict reporting, as the spread of misinformation and disinformation becomes the biggest threat to credible news.

The NBC has nominated one of its senior journalists for the War Journalism Training Programme in Türkiye this month.

The geographic isolation of PNG and the Pacific shields the region from the direct conflict risks faced by other nations.

The region however, faces growing risks when reporting in difficult disaster zones.

Speaking on a panel during the Asia Pacific Union Global News Leaders forum underway in Sydney, ABU Group News Chair and Deputy Director General of Turkish Radio and Television [TRT] Ahmet Gormez said newsrooms globally face mounting challenges in getting the truth out in difficult conflict areas.

He warned that beyond physical danger, there is an information war being waged alongside conflicts.

He said newsrooms are now prioritizing efforts to combat lies and disinformation while managing shrinking budgets.

Mr. Gormez also said the survival of journalists and the human role in storytelling must be protected, even as media funding and regulation remain major challenges.

He said despite advances in technology, news must continue to be reported by people on the ground.

"We are called journalists because we are living in this time zone of humanity. I really think it's very important. History needs to be written by human beings.

The comments come during discussions about how public broadcasters can remain resilient amid financial pressure, Artificial Intelligence, misinformation, and competition from commercial media.

Meanwhile, acting Director of the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) News, Donna Field, said the biggest challenge for news leaders today is breaking through a crowded media landscape to reach audiences.

Speaking on the same panel, she said the focus remains on protecting public interest journalism.

"The fact that it is a crowded environment now, trying to get people's attention."

According to the acting Director of ABC News, newsrooms can no longer rely on the old model where a good story will find its audience.

"We have to do a lot of strategic thinking about how we get to audiences now….something we perhaps didn't have to do 30, 40, 50 years ago. In terms of the ways we tell stories, the platforms and the formats, these are critically important."

She warned that ensuring the legacy of public interest journalism remains a challenge..

"In a world where political sands are shifting, where there is mis- and disinformation, where journalists are often a target, these are really challenging things for news organisations around the world.”

Papua New Guinea is facing a rising tide of online misinformation and disinformation.

The Department of Information and Communications Technology is actively implementing policies and digital frameworks to combat the problem.

item.title: Literacy curriculum to empower rural communities
item.description: The Anglican Church of PNG has showcased Katima Literacy School in Northern Province as its model school under a new nine-month literacy curriculum aimed at empowering rural communities. Speaking during National Literacy Week, Anglican Church Partnership Program Coordinator, Michael Ambo said the church’s literacy program began in 2004.
item.content:encoded:
The Anglican Church of PNG has showcased Katima Literacy School in Northern Province as its model school under a new nine-month literacy curriculum aimed at empowering rural communities.

Speaking during National Literacy Week, Anglican Church Partnership Program Coordinator, Michael Ambo said the church’s literacy program began in 2004.

“It was a long and challenging journey. We established a lot of schools, and we had 132 literacy schools,” Ambo said.

The 132 schools were set up not only in Popondetta but across five provinces where the Anglican Church operates, including Northern, Milne Bay, Western Highlands and Port Moresby.

In 2023, the Anglican Church developed the Melanesian Empowering Literacy for All curriculum. The program runs for nine months and covers basic literacy, post-literacy and practical skills.

“In this curriculum we have the basic and post literacy, and that is what we have been teaching,” he said.

Katima Literacy School has been selected as the model school for the curriculum.

Ambo said the school also runs an economic empowerment model in partnership with the Division of Agriculture and Livestock. The pilot project focuses on smart agriculture, climate change and SME development. As part of the initiative, rice and cocoa farms have been established at Katima.

The curriculum also addresses cross-cutting issues such as social accountability, gender equality and social inclusion, and child protection.

“Through this curriculum we have a success of learners who have gone into self-employment. Community empowerment, people are able to engage meaningfully in society,” he said.

He confirmed that two batches of learners have already graduated from Katima Literacy School and are now taking the lead in community activities.

Ambo thanked the National Department of Education, partners and stakeholders for their support. He called for increased funding and resources for community-based literacy programs.

“Literacy is the key to solving any issues, whether economic or social issues in PNG. We have to put more funds and resources to literacy, because this is a community-based initiative that will change people’s lives,” he said.

He also acknowledged the Australian Government through the PNGAus Partnership, the PNG Church Partnership Program, and the Building Community Engagement in PNG, or BCEP program, for providing funding to the Anglican Church of PNG to strengthen inclusive literacy work.

item.title: Fly-River shipping operations likely to be disrupted
item.description: The Fly River at Kiunga has started to fall after reaching a peak of seven (7) meters over the weekend following good rainfall in the Upper Fly and Ok Tedi catchments. According to Ok Tedi Mining Limited Kiunga Operations, data issued at 10am today, Tuesday 2nd September 2026, shows that the river has dropped to 5.080 meters and is classified as "extremely low" and continues to fall.
item.content:encoded:
The Fly River at Kiunga has started to fall after reaching a peak of seven (7) meters over the weekend following good rainfall in the Upper Fly and Ok Tedi catchments.

According to Ok Tedi Mining Limited Kiunga Operations, data issued at 10am today, Tuesday 2nd September 2026, shows that the river has dropped to 5.080 meters and is classified as "extremely low" and continues to fall.

OTML Kiunga Operations further stated that the PNG National Weather Service is forecasting only isolated showers and thunderstorms for today and tomorrow with 1-30mm of rain. From Friday to Sunday, lighter isolated showers of 10mm or less are expected.

Officials from OTML Kiunga Operations said with low rainfall expected in the coming days, river levels are likely to drop further. This will likely disrupt the movements of shipping vessels up and down the Fly River system.

According to the National Weather Service, below average rainfall is predicted for the Ok Tedi and Upper Fly catchments for September, October and November due to the current strong El Niño.

OTML Kiunga Operations is advising communities and shipping operators along the Fly River to take note of the changing conditions.

item.title: Down-scaling of services at Madang Provincial Hospital to continue for another 2 weeks
item.description: The downscaling of services at the Madang Provincial Hospital will continue for another two weeks, according to the hospital's Acting Executive Manager, Jeremiah Johnmark. In a media conference today, Mr. Johnmark confirmed that vital medical supplies at the hospital have increased to at least 13. 8 per cent from the previous 5 per cent after the National Health Department through the Area Medica
item.content:encoded:
The downscaling of services at the Madang Provincial Hospital will continue for another two weeks, according to the hospital's Acting Executive Manager, Jeremiah Johnmark.

In a media conference today, Mr. Johnmark confirmed that vital medical supplies at the hospital have increased to at least 13. 8 per cent from the previous 5 per cent after the National Health Department through the Area Medica Store supplied some of the essential medical drugs that the hospital did not have.

Unfortunately, he clarified that this is still not enough to guarantee the uplifting of the temporary down- scaling of services at the hospital.

"Until we've received 50 per cent or more, we remain in scale down mode for the next two weeks. But we are hopeful that during this time, we should receive some more supplies," Mr Johnmark said.

The hospital began scaling down services on August 13 due to a critical shortage in vital medical drugs and consumables.

"We made the decision to scale down because in the last six months of this year, we only received 5 per cent of the total medical drugs and consumables that we've ordered 95 per cent of the 6 000 plus items were outstanding.

"In the last two weeks, the National Health Department through the Area Medical Store in Lae was able to supply all the essential medicines and consumables that we did not have in stock.

"I want to take this time to also thank the National Health Department, especially the Medical Supplies Branch, for listening to our hospital's cries, our staff, patients, and the general public in the last two weeks. He said.

He said for the next two-week Madang provincial hospital will give time for the NDoH and the Area Medical Store in Lae to find ways to supply their critical stocks of medicine.

"We hope that in the next two weeks we should beef up our stock level to 50 per cent or more. By then we should uplift the scale down and return to normal services," he said.

Meanwhile, Johnmark extended the hospital's appreciation to the general public for their understanding at this very critical time.

item.title: Voice of Revival Radio and Television launched in Port Moresby
item.description: A long-awaited dream is now a reality for the Revival Centers of Papua New Guinea with the official launch of its Voice of Revival digital radio and television station in Port Moresby on Tuesday. The launch coincided with the church’s 44th Anniversary celebrations and was held under the theme “His Voice, Our Voice, Their Voice, the Voice of Revival.”
item.content:encoded:
A long-awaited dream is now a reality for the Revival Centers of Papua New Guinea with the official launch of its Voice of Revival digital radio and television station in Port Moresby on Tuesday.

The launch coincided with the church’s 44th Anniversary celebrations and was held under the theme “His Voice, Our Voice, Their Voice, the Voice of Revival.”

What is now a modern broadcast center was once the church Principal Pastor’s unused office.

The idea to revive a radio station, first announced in 1997, was brought back to life in 2022.

An initial cost of K500,000 was estimated. After prayer and planning, the church began working with the National Information and Communication Technology Authority, NICTA.

Construction started in 2024 and faced challenges with funding, skills and infrastructure.

But with support from the church, congregations, and technical teams from Australia, the facility was completed. It now operates as both a podcast and broadcast center, able to go live on radio and camera.

The station was officially launched on Tuesday, September 1st, 2026 by Founder and Principal Pastor Godfrey Wippon.

NICTA CEO Lume Polume commended the church for using technology to expand the gospel, saying it aligns with government policy.

He urged the church to use the service responsibly and not discriminate against others.

Chief Censor Jim Abani also said content aired on the station must be decent for public consumption.

A radio station certificate was presented during the launch, officially recognizing Voice of Revival as a broadcaster.

Meanwhile, Deputy Managing Director for NBC Michael Samuga pledged NBC’s support towards the newly established Voice of Revival Radio and Digital Television Station.

The platform will now be used to spread the Gospel and the truth, and to reach communities across PNG and beyond.

item.title: Police launch probe into early morning gold robbery
item.description: A major police investigation is underway following an early morning heist in Port Moresby where 10 armed men ambushed a private security convoy and escaped with gold bullion, cash, and firearms. Police Commissioner David Manning confirmed that the armed robbery occurred around 4:30am on Wednesday when two private security vehicles carrying the commercial shipment were intercepted by unknown vehicl
item.content:encoded:
A major police investigation is underway following an early morning heist in Port Moresby where 10 armed men ambushed a private security convoy and escaped with gold bullion, cash, and firearms.

Police Commissioner David Manning confirmed that the armed robbery occurred around 4:30am on Wednesday when two private security vehicles carrying the commercial shipment were intercepted by unknown vehicles.

The heavily armed assailants held the private security personnel at gunpoint before seizing the consignment of gold bullion, cash, and firearms.

Deputy Commissioner of Specialist Operations Donald Yamasombi has been appointed to direct the probe. Investigators are currently interviewing eyewitnesses, security crew members, and management from the security firm.

Manning expressed serious concerns regarding the operation of the private security firm, revealing that police were not informed prior to the high-value transport.

“The gold and cash were being carried by a private security firm and police had not been alerted to the movement prior to it taking place,” Manning said.

“Police are not privy to the standard operating procedures of private security businesses that are contracted to carry commercial valuables.

“This is a very serious incident. Early indications are that the movement of these valuables by the security company leave a lot to be desired in terms of how the private operation was conducted.”

Manning said both the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] and private clients expect the highest level of professional conduct from security management and staff.

He assured that the priority for RPNGC investigators remains the prompt identification of the suspects, the recovery of the stolen property, and a full review of the security firm’s standard procedures.

item.title: Public broadcasters to do more
item.description: The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) Managing Director Hugh Marks said that while the national broadcaster can now reach more Australians than ever before, it is being asked to "do more without more" across an expanding range of platforms.

item.title: Media urged to be steadfast
item.description: Traditional media is undergoing rapid change, but public broadcasters must remain steadfast in delivering credible news, especially during times of conflict, disaster, and uncertainty.
